task.description:
Validate the CODE-DESIGNER Step 01 design for DDL-02, ORD-01, ORD-02, ORD-04. Standard checks apply. Additionally: verify the design's claim that src/effects/worker.zig/queue.zig is a genuine, correctly-cited existing FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED pattern to follow (read those files yourself). Verify the design's argument that ORD-02's per-correlation advisory lock is NOT redundant with SKIP LOCKED (unlike a previously-removed per-timer lock referenced as ISS-301 precedent) -- read that precedent/history if cited and confirm the distinction is sound, since getting this backwards would mean reintroducing a documented anti-pattern. Verify DDL-02 correctly extends ddl_validate.zig's existing ValidatePlatformDDL pipeline rather than creating a parallel validator. Check if docs/processes/system/effect-reentry-ordering.md (cited by the designer as an authoritative process spec for PW-07) genuinely exists and the design is consistent with it.

RE-VALIDATION (after REWORK 1): CODE-DESIGNER added file/byte_offset fields to StatementDescriptor (ddl_validate.zig) and ConstrainBeforeExpandDetail, and confirmed ddl_namespace.zig (DDL-05) is unaffected since checkNamespace is called with an anonymous struct literal, not the shared StatementDescriptor directly. Re-verify this claim and that AC5 is now genuinely covered.
acceptance_criteria: Every AC in DDL-02, ORD-01, ORD-02, ORD-04 traced to a design section
No implementation code in the design
DDL-02 extends the existing validator pipeline correctly
ORD-02 lock-non-redundancy argument verified sound against the cited ISS-301/removed-lock precedent

result.summary: RE-VALIDATION after REWORK 1: DDL-02 AC5 is now genuinely covered. Independently confirmed in src/platform/ddl_validate.zig that the sole call site of ddl_namespace.checkNamespace (line 179) passes an anonymous 3-field struct literal (.kind/.object_name/.previous_object_name copied from stmt), never the StatementDescriptor value itself, so the added file/byte_offset fields on ddl_validate.StatementDescriptor cannot reach ddl_namespace.checkNamespace or its own differently-shaped, same-named StatementDescriptor type. Grepped the whole src/ tree: no other call site of checkNamespace or reference to ddl_namespace.StatementDescriptor exists outside ddl_namespace.zig itself, whose own test blocks construct that type directly and are unaffected. Design doc now specifies constraining_statement_file/byte_offset and depended_on_statement_file/byte_offset on ConstrainBeforeExpandDetail, matching AC5 verbatim (docs/requirements.yaml DDL-02 body). Rework diff (5540e73d..1ccc6b56) touches only the DDL-02 design doc plus handoff/registry/log bookkeeping -- ORD-01/02/04 design doc and both migration YAMLs are byte-identical, confirming no scope creep. tools/lint_design_artefact.py on the updated doc: OK, 0 issues. All other findings from the original Step 1b review (DDL-02 extends validatePlatformDDL correctly, worker.zig/queue.zig SKIP LOCKED citation, ORD-02 advisory-lock non-redundancy vs. ISS-301, effect-reentry-ordering.md consistency) are unchanged by this rework and remain valid.
